---
title: "DataSHIELD packages"
description: "How the test suggestions test DataSHIELD client and utility packages, against an in-process DSLite server where needed."
---

Client-side functions of a DataSHIELD package need a DataSHIELD server to
run. With `datashield: true`, the [test suggestions](test-suggest.qmd)
run such tests against [DSLite](https://github.com/datashield/DSLite), an
in-process server. Which functions that applies to depends on
`datashield-type`:

| `datashield-type` | Tested against DSLite | Other functions |
|---|---|---|
| `client` | every function | — |
| `utility` | functions that work on DataSHIELD connections: a `datasources` argument, or `datashield.*()` / `ds.*()` calls | tested locally, see below |
| `server` | — | tested like any R package |

Any other value stops the run with an error, so a typo can't silently
change the testing strategy.

## The DSLite setup

- An **existing DSLite setup** in any `tests/testthat/setup*.R` or
  `helper*.R` is reused, with your own connection names, symbols and
  helpers.
- Otherwise one is **created** with one of DSLite's bundled datasets, in
  `tests/testthat/setup.R`, or in `setup-dslite.R` if a `setup.R`
  without DSLite already exists. Your `setup.R` is never touched.

Claude sees the structure of the test data inside the DSLite server, see
[what Claude gets](test-suggest-review.qmd#what-claude-gets).

::: {.callout-important}
DSLite takes the server functions from the **installed server packages**.
List them (e.g. `dsBase`), together with `DSLite` and `testthat`, in your
`DESCRIPTION`, for example under `Suggests`, so the workflow installs
them. Otherwise every test fails as `env_misconfiguration`.
:::

## Utility packages {#utility}

Utility packages help the analyst rather than wrap a server function: they
set up analysis projects, create mock data or manage packages. Their
functions that don't work on connections are tested for real on the local
machine:

- **In a temporary directory** (`withr::local_tempdir()`, or your
  setup's own temporary paths), never in the user's home or working
  directory;
- **Asserting on the return value and on the files** the function creates
  and their content;
- **Mocking only what must not run in a test:** installing packages,
  network access or opening an RStudio project, with
  `testthat::local_mocked_bindings()`;
- **Using your setup files' objects and settings**, e.g. a test
  configuration read in `setup.R`.
